title: This is Peak Bulk (Hypertrophy Log #6)
summary: NH shows a lower day and an upper day from his new program in his basement home gym. Lower: deep rounded rack hinges, tibialis raises, belt-squat split squats, belt calf raises, grippers and front-neck work. Upper: pronation curls, rear delt rehab, chest-supported Kroc rows, JM presses, upright rows with a wrist roller and strict reverse curls. He rates his physique peak bulk after a slow 10 lb gain in two years.
claims: His basement gym has a 6'4 ceiling, so he trains legs and some isolation at home and overhead work at a commercial gym
A deep barbell hinge from a rack where the upper back dives past the hips and the lumbar spine rounds is safe at a slow tempo and hammers the erectors
He avoided tibialis raises because they were hard to standardize until he got a machine; slow negatives and a big stretch, 15-20 reps with drop sets
His calves are close to 18.5 inches and he thinks his build needs 21-22 inches to look huge; he trains them hard three times a week
He trains legs three times a week with only 3-4 sets for quads or hamstrings per session
He plateaued on split squats because balance with dumbbells was the limit; belt-squat split squats with hands free fixed it
Belt-squat split squats keep you vertical and are almost pure quad, good for VMO but not for glutes
Any lower-body movement has grown his glutes; he doesn't need to target them
Think as a bodybuilder: use your energy to get the most stimulus possible
Belt-squat calf raises load the pelvis rather than the spine and give a better stretch; slow tempo, heels never touch
He closed a 2.0 Captains of Crush gripper easily and nearly closed the 2.5 cold
Plate-on-head neck curls become grip work past about 90 lb; instead do front-neck work lying against a preacher with the weight hanging from a harness
Use slow tempo and be ready to catch the harness; pick a weight you can do 10 reps with, then pause reps
Pronation curls: loop deep in the hand, control and stretch the negative supinated, pronate on the way up; 40 lb for 12 is hard for him
His shoulders and traps improved strictly through isolation and taking presses more seriously
He gained 10 lb in two years while keeping a visible six-pack
Plan: only cut if he competes; otherwise maintain in summer and slow bulk in winter
Constant PRs keep him in love with the gym
Rear delt/external rotation work fixed his posterior shoulder pain from pressing; keep rehab movements in even when pain is gone
He believes the next five years will be his most productive for gains
Kroc rows chest-supported on a preacher bench keep the torso vertical for traps and rhomboids rather than lats; emphasize the stretch
Start unilateral work with the weaker side; humans aren't symmetrical, so slight form differences are fine
JM press with an SSB or Smith machine fully rehabbed his elbow tendinitis; bring the bar to neck level and punch through the triceps
When JM press form fails, rest the bar on the safeties and continue with partial skullcrushers
Upright rows with a wrist roller handle let the wrists move freely and helped his shoulder pain; use about 30 lb for 10-20 reps
His old wide-grip partial reverse curls with 150 lb were ego lifting; now strapped, full range with a 1 s squeeze, then thumbless once failing
Small forearms are not a lifelong curse; train them directly and they grow
exercises: slow tempo, let upper back dive past hips
slow negative, big stretch, 15-20 reps, drop sets
hands free for balance, vertical torso, knee forward
weight hanging from harness, slow tempo
front neck stretch without grip limits
torso vertical, rotate into the stretch
SSB or Smith; bar to neck; skullcrusher motion
Upright row with wrist roller handle
straps, thumb around, squeeze at top, then thumbless
